cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Weather Watchers Circle
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Observe outdoors/window weather and record it on the class chart.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Children look outside, describe sky/air, and place a weather symbol on today’s chart square.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.materials:
Weather chart
Symbol cards (printable)
Window/door access
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.preparation:
Post chart at child height
Prep today’s blank square
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Look outside together
2. Share what you notice (sky, wet, wind)
3. Choose a weather symbol
4. Mark warm/cool with a simple choice
5. Predict tomorrow in one word
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: What do you observe about today’s weather?
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.observationOpportunities: Describes weather; places symbol; uses weather words.
teacherTips: Do this daily — repetition builds the science habit.
observationPrompts: Describes weather; places symbol; uses weather words.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.imageBriefSetup: Child-height weather chart by window with symbol cards.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Sunshine Movement Game
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Move like sunshine with big stretches and shadow play when possible.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Children stretch like sun rays, move fast/slow, and notice shadows if sunny.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.preparation:
Clear space
If sunny, note shadow wall/floor
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Stretch arms like sun rays
2. Move slowly then quickly
3. Make shadows if sunny
4. Drink water after moving
5. Rest in shade pretend spot
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: Can your arms shine like warm sun rays?
teacherTips: On cloudy days, use flashlight shadow play indoors.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Cloudy Day Process Art
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Explore cloudy-day materials in an open-ended art invitation.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Children use cotton, chalk, paint, or torn paper on blue/gray paper however they choose — no sample cloud to copy.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.materials:
Blue/gray paper
Cotton/fiber fill
Chalk
White paint
Sponges
Glue sticks
Smocks
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.preparation:
Set materials buffet
Prompt: ‘How does a cloudy sky feel/look?’
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.setup: Art table invitation without model product.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Feel/choose materials
2. Explore on paper your own way
3. Add more layers if you want
4. Describe your weather art
5. Dry and display all styles together
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: What happens when you try two materials together?
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.observationOpportunities: Makes choices; stays with process; uses weather words.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.safetyNotes: Supervise glue; avoid inhaling loose fibers.
teacherTips: If every piece looks different, you did it right.
observationPrompts: Makes choices; stays with process; uses weather words.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.imageBriefSetup: Cloudy-day art invitation tray with mixed materials — no finished sample cloud.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Rain Drop Sensory Investigate
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Investigate water ‘rain’ with tools and describe how it moves.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Children drip, pour, and splash in a shallow rain bin using cups, eyedroppers, and waterproof figures.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.materials:
Shallow water bin
Cups
Eyedroppers/basters
Towels
Smocks
Optional rain stick
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.preparation:
Fill shallow water
Towel floor
Limit participants
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Listen to rain stick or rain sounds talk
2. Drip water like rain
3. Pour from high/low — what changes?
4. Use words wet/splash/drip
5. Dry hands and reset tools
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: What do you notice when the rain falls from higher up?
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.observationOpportunities: Pours with control; uses descriptive words; collaborates.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.safetyNotes: Shallow water only; mop spills; no drinking bin water.
teacherTips: Add ice on hot days for temperature talk.
observationPrompts: Pours with control; uses descriptive words; collaborates.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.imageBriefSetup: Shallow rain sensory bin with cups and droppers.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Weather Dress-Up Center
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Choose clothing/gear that matches called weather scenarios.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Children dress for sunny, rainy, windy, or cold play scenarios using real/play gear.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.materials:
Raincoats
Boots
Hats
Sunglasses
Scarves
Weather cards
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.preparation:
Sort gear into bins by type
Post weather cards
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Draw/choose a weather card
2. Pick gear that fits
3. Explain your choice
4. Act out a weather day
5. Hang gear back
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: What do you wear when it is windy and cool?
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.observationOpportunities: Matches gear to weather; explains; role plays.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.safetyNotes: No drawstring hazards; trip-aware with oversized boots.
teacherTips: Include inclusive clothing options.
observationPrompts: Matches gear to weather; explains; role plays.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.imageBriefSetup: Weather dress-up center with labeled gear bins and weather cards.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Windy Day Pinwheel Lab
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Test what moves in wind using pinwheels, scarves, and teacher-controlled air.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Children compare how different objects move when they blow, wave, or use a safe teacher-held fan.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.materials:
Pinwheels
Scarves
Paper
Feathers (large)
Teacher-controlled fan optional
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.preparation:
Outdoor breeze preferred
If fan used, teacher holds only
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.setup: Wind lab table or outdoor spot.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Predict which item will move most
2. Test by blowing/waving
3. Try scarf vs paper
4. Optional teacher fan test
5. Share what you noticed
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.observationOpportunities: Predicts; tests; compares; uses wind words.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.safetyNotes: Teacher holds fan; keep fingers away; no pointing fan at faces close-up.
teacherTips: Document with photos of moving scarves for family board.
observationPrompts: Predicts; tests; compares; uses wind words.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.imageBriefSetup: Wind investigation with pinwheels and scarves on a tray.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Weather Chart Helpers
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Help update the week chart and count weather types so far.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Chart helpers mark today and count how many sunny/rainy/etc. days are recorded.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Review days already marked
2. Add today’s symbol
3. Count each weather type
4. Which has more?
5. Choose tomorrow’s helpers
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: How many rainy days do we have so far?
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.observationOpportunities: Counts with 1:1; compares quantities; takes helper role.
teacherTips: Graph talk beats perfect counting.
observationPrompts: Counts with 1:1; compares quantities; takes helper role.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Thunder Drum Experiment
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Explore loud/soft storm sounds safely and talk about storm feelings/safety.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Children compare drum/pan sounds as ‘thunder’ play, then practice calm-down and indoor-safety talk.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.materials:
Drums
Metal pans
Mallets
Soft scarves for calm-down
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.preparation:
Warn sensitive children
Offer quiet corner
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Practice soft taps
2. Try louder taps (still safe)
3. Compare which sounds like far/near thunder
4. Talk storm safety (go indoors)
5. Calm with slow breathing and scarves
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: Thunder is loud — what helps your body feel safe?
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.observationOpportunities: Controls volume; discusses feelings; recalls safety.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.safetyNotes: Ear-aware; no banging near faces; stop if distressed.
teacherTips: Pair science with SEL for storms.
observationPrompts: Controls volume; discusses feelings; recalls safety.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.imageBriefSetup: Sound exploration circle with drums/pans and calm-down scarves.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Weather Book Nook
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Explore weather books and retell a weather event with pictures.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Children browse weather books and use props/cards to retell rain, wind, or snow moments.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.materials:
Weather books
Story props
Retell cards
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Choose a weather book
2. Look for weather clues in pictures
3. Retell with a prop
4. Share one new weather word
5. Reshelve book
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: What weather did you find in the pictures?
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.observationOpportunities: Attends to book; retells; uses vocab.
teacherTips: Pair a hesitant reader with picture walk only.
observationPrompts: Attends to book; retells; uses vocab.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Clothing and Season Sort
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Sort clothing/season cards by weather needs and talk about local seasons.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Children sort picture cards of clothing and seasonal scenes into weather trays.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.preparation: Label trays sunny/rainy/cold/windy or seasons as fits climate
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Name tray labels
2. Pick a card
3. Sort and explain
4. Resort one card if you change your mind
5. Count a tray
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: Why does this clothing fit that weather?
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.observationOpportunities: Sorts with reason; flexible thinking; counts.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.safetyNotes: Cards laminated; no small choking pieces.
teacherTips: Adapt seasons to your local climate.
observationPrompts: Sorts with reason; flexible thinking; counts.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.imageBriefSetup: Sorting trays with clothing and weather picture cards.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Weather Colors Process Painting
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Paint weather ideas with color choices and tools children select.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Children paint sunny, rainy, windy, or stormy feelings/colors with brushes, sponges, or fingers — results vary.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.materials:
Tempera paints
Paper
Brushes/sponges
Smocks
Optional spray bottles with water
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.preparation:
Limited palette + open tools
No rainbow sample chart to copy
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.setup: Painting easels/table with weather word cards as optional inspiration.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Choose weather idea
2. Pick colors/tools
3. Paint your way
4. Optional water spray for rainy effects
5. Title your work with a weather word
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: What colors feel like today’s weather?
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.observationOpportunities: Chooses tools; stays with process; connects to weather.
teacherTips: Skip ‘rainbow order’ instructions entirely.
observationPrompts: Chooses tools; stays with process; connects to weather.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.imageBriefSetup: Painting setup with mixed tools and weather word cards — no model rainbow.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Weather Yoga and Rest
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Practice calm weather-themed stretches and rest.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Children move through gentle sun, cloud, and rain poses, then rest.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Reach for sun pose
2. Float like cloud pose
3. Gentle rain finger taps
4. Lie still like a calm day
5. Breathe slowly together
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: Let your body feel calm like quiet weather.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.observationOpportunities: Follows gentle poses; rests; slow breathing.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.safetyNotes: No forced stretches; respect body limits.
teacherTips: Useful after thunder sound play.
observationPrompts: Follows gentle poses; rests; slow breathing.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Meteorologist Report Circle
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Give a short weather report using the class chart.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Children take turns as meteorologists with a pointer/mic prop describing chart weather.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.materials:
Pointer
Chart
Microphone prop
Symbol cards
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Point to today’s symbol
2. Say weather words
3. Share one clothing tip
4. Optional weekend guess
5. Pass mic to next reporter
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: You’re on the weather report — what should friends wear?
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.observationOpportunities: Speaks to group; uses chart; clothing connection.
teacherTips: Allow buddy reporting for shy children.
observationPrompts: Speaks to group; uses chart; clothing connection.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Weather Dress Relay
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Choose correct gear for called weather and move safely in a relay.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: When a weather type is called, children grab one matching gear item and tag a friend — careful over fast.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.preparation:
Three clear gear piles
Demonstrate safe tagging
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Call a weather type
2. Child chooses one matching item
3. Move to cone and tag next friend
4. Switch weather calls
5. Review choices together
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: Careful helpers pick the right gear!
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.safetyNotes: No knock-down racing; spot for boots trips.
teacherTips: Praise accuracy over speed.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.imageBriefSetup: Relay with three weather gear piles and cones.

cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.title: Weather Watchers Celebration
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.objective: Review the week’s weather data and celebrate investigations.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.description: Class counts chart data, thanks chart helpers, sings, and shares favorite activities.
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.materials:
Completed chart
Song list
Optional photos of investigations
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.steps:
1. Count weather types for the week
2. Thank chart helpers
3. Sing Weather Watchers Song
4. Share favorite investigation
5. Send family weather-watch reminder
cur-lp-preschool-weather-watchers:item-p.teacherLanguage: What weather did we see most this week?
teacherTips: Connect celebration to real observing habit at home.

week.weeklyOverview: Preschoolers become weather watchers who observe, record, and investigate sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, and stormy weather. Clothing choices, safety, and process art support real outdoor noticing — not elementary meteorology worksheets.
week.objectives:
Observe and describe daily weather using child-friendly vocabulary
Record weather on a simple class chart
Investigate wind, water, and sound through play experiments
Connect weather to clothing and safety choices
Express weather ideas through process art and movement
week.weeklyMaterials:
Weather chart + symbol cards (printable draft)
Clipboards
Pinwheels / scarves / small fan (teacher-controlled)
Water/rain sensory bin tools
Dress-up weather gear
Paint, paper, cotton/cloud materials for process art
Drums/metal pans for thunder sound play
Season/clothing cards (printable draft)
Books about weather
week.familyConnection: Families can share one weather observation at drop-off for the class chart (photo optional).
week.adaptations: Use real photos for support. Indoor alternatives for extreme weather. Accept one-word weather descriptions. Offer hand-over-hand for chart marking.
week.vocabularyWords:
sunny
rainy
cloudy
windy
storm
warm
cold
observe
forecast
cloud
wind
temperature
safe
week.teacherPreparation:
Post weather chart at child height near window/door
Print weather/clothing cards (draft)
Stage wind and rain investigation trays

Books about weather

monday.outdoorPlay: Outdoor weather walk with clipboards (shade/safe conditions).

monday.safetyNotes: Never observe lightning outdoors. Teacher-controlled fans only. Supervise water play. Allergy-aware art materials.

items.title: Thunder Drum Experiment
items.objective: Explore loud/soft storm sounds safely and talk about storm feelings/safety.
items.description: Children compare drum/pan sounds as ‘thunder’ play, then practice calm-down and indoor-safety talk.
items.materials:
Drums
Metal pans
Mallets
Soft scarves for calm-down
items.preparation:
Warn sensitive children
Offer quiet corner
items.steps:
1. Practice soft taps
2. Try louder taps (still safe)
3. Compare which sounds like far/near thunder
4. Talk storm safety (go indoors)
5. Calm with slow breathing and scarves
items.teacherLanguage: Thunder is loud — what helps your body feel safe?
items.observationOpportunities: Controls volume; discusses feelings; recalls safety.
items.safetyNotes: Ear-aware; no banging near faces; stop if distressed.
teacherTips: Pair science with SEL for storms.
items.imageBriefSetup: Sound exploration circle with drums/pans and calm-down scarves.

items.title: Weather Book Nook
items.objective: Explore weather books and retell a weather event with pictures.
items.description: Children browse weather books and use props/cards to retell rain, wind, or snow moments.
items.materials:
Weather books
Story props
Retell cards
items.steps:
1. Choose a weather book
2. Look for weather clues in pictures
3. Retell with a prop
4. Share one new weather word
5. Reshelve book
items.teacherLanguage: What weather did you find in the pictures?
items.observationOpportunities: Attends to book; retells; uses vocab.
teacherTips: Pair a hesitant reader with picture walk only.

warm

observe
forecast

thursday.outdoorPlay: Shadow/sun play if sunny; puddle look if rainy and safe.
thursday.adaptations: Use real photos for support. Indoor alternatives for extreme weather. Accept one-word weather descriptions. Offer hand-over-hand for chart marking.
thursday.safetyNotes: Never observe lightning outdoors. Teacher-controlled fans only. Supervise water play. Allergy-aware art materials.

items.title: Clothing and Season Sort
items.objective: Sort clothing/season cards by weather needs and talk about local seasons.
items.description: Children sort picture cards of clothing and seasonal scenes into weather trays.
items.preparation: Label trays sunny/rainy/cold/windy or seasons as fits climate
items.steps:
1. Name tray labels
2. Pick a card
3. Sort and explain
4. Resort one card if you change your mind
5. Count a tray
items.teacherLanguage: Why does this clothing fit that weather?
items.observationOpportunities: Sorts with reason; flexible thinking; counts.
items.safetyNotes: Cards laminated; no small choking pieces.
teacherTips: Adapt seasons to your local climate.
items.imageBriefSetup: Sorting trays with clothing and weather picture cards.

items.title: Weather Colors Process Painting
items.objective: Paint weather ideas with color choices and tools children select.
items.description: Children paint sunny, rainy, windy, or stormy feelings/colors with brushes, sponges, or fingers — results vary.
items.materials:
Tempera paints
Paper
Brushes/sponges
Smocks
Optional spray bottles with water
items.preparation:
Limited palette + open tools
No rainbow sample chart to copy
items.setup: Painting easels/table with weather word cards as optional inspiration.
items.steps:
1. Choose weather idea
2. Pick colors/tools
3. Paint your way
4. Optional water spray for rainy effects
5. Title your work with a weather word
items.teacherLanguage: What colors feel like today’s weather?
items.observationOpportunities: Chooses tools; stays with process; connects to weather.
teacherTips: Skip ‘rainbow order’ instructions entirely.
items.imageBriefSetup: Painting setup with mixed tools and weather word cards — no model rainbow.

items.title: Weather Yoga and Rest
items.objective: Practice calm weather-themed stretches and rest.
items.description: Children move through gentle sun, cloud, and rain poses, then rest.
items.steps:
1. Reach for sun pose
2. Float like cloud pose
3. Gentle rain finger taps
4. Lie still like a calm day
5. Breathe slowly together
items.teacherLanguage: Let your body feel calm like quiet weather.
items.observationOpportunities: Follows gentle poses; rests; slow breathing.
items.safetyNotes: No forced stretches; respect body limits.
teacherTips: Useful after thunder sound play.

items.title: Meteorologist Report Circle
items.objective: Give a short weather report using the class chart.
items.description: Children take turns as meteorologists with a pointer/mic prop describing chart weather.
items.materials:
Pointer
Chart
Microphone prop
Symbol cards
items.steps:
1. Point to today’s symbol
2. Say weather words
3. Share one clothing tip
4. Optional weekend guess
5. Pass mic to next reporter
items.teacherLanguage: You’re on the weather report — what should friends wear?
items.observationOpportunities: Speaks to group; uses chart; clothing connection.
teacherTips: Allow buddy reporting for shy children.

items.title: Weather Dress Relay
items.objective: Choose correct gear for called weather and move safely in a relay.
items.description: When a weather type is called, children grab one matching gear item and tag a friend — careful over fast.
items.preparation:
Three clear gear piles
Demonstrate safe tagging
items.steps:
1. Call a weather type
2. Child chooses one matching item
3. Move to cone and tag next friend
4. Switch weather calls
5. Review choices together
items.teacherLanguage: Careful helpers pick the right gear!
items.safetyNotes: No knock-down racing; spot for boots trips.
teacherTips: Praise accuracy over speed.
items.imageBriefSetup: Relay with three weather gear piles and cones.

items.title: Weather Watchers Celebration
items.objective: Review the week’s weather data and celebrate investigations.
items.description: Class counts chart data, thanks chart helpers, sings, and shares favorite activities.
items.materials:
Completed chart
Song list
Optional photos of investigations
items.steps:
1. Count weather types for the week
2. Thank chart helpers
3. Sing Weather Watchers Song
4. Share favorite investigation
5. Send family weather-watch reminder
items.teacherLanguage: What weather did we see most this week?
teacherTips: Connect celebration to real observing habit at home.

songs.title: Weather Watchers Song (LLH original)
songs.lyrics:
Look outside, what do you see?
Sunny, cloudy, windy, rainy as can be.
We observe and then we say,
What’s the weather for today?
songs.motions: Point outside; act each weather word.

songs.title: Wind on My Face (LLH original)
songs.lyrics:
Wind on my face, wind in my hair,
Scarves and pinwheels spinning in the air.
Blow, blow, gently today,
Watch how the wind moves things away.
